predictedRisks.riskTitle: Contract Extension Approval and Amendment Not Formalized
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project timeline extends 49 days beyond the contractual end date of September 11, 2026, reaching October 30, 2026, without documented formal contract amendment or extension approval. This creates legal exposure, payment ambiguity for work performed beyond the original term, and potential service level agreement gaps during the extended period.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Original 16-week contract baseline did not account for comprehensive testing phases (PAT, Regression), deployment preparation, training, and hypercare support. Historical pattern shows regression testing and extended PAT were added after project initiation without formal SOW amendment, creating governance precedent for scope expansion without contractual alignment.

Payment milestone 6 (Deployment - Week 14) and milestone 7 (Hypercare - Weeks 15-16) occur beyond contract term
Service delivery extends into October 2026 without formal coverage

potentialImpact.schedule: No direct schedule impact as extension is already planned, but lack of formal approval creates uncertainty and potential for abrupt termination
potentialImpact.cost: Payment terms for extended period unclear; potential disputes over milestone payments 6 and 7 totaling $36,300; risk of uncompensated work or cost overrun claims
potentialImpact.quality: Service level agreements and acceptance criteria may not apply beyond contract term, creating quality accountability gaps
potentialImpact.customer: Stakeholder confidence erosion due to contractual ambiguity; potential relationship damage if payment or service disputes arise; delayed business value realization
potentialImpact.operations: Legal and compliance exposure; insurance coverage gaps; resource commitment uncertainty; governance framework validity beyond contract term unclear

predictedRisks.reasoning: The risk is highly likely because the project is already operating 11 weeks into a 16-week contract with 12 weeks of remaining work planned. Historical evidence shows the same client experienced governance drift when testing phases were added post-initiation without SOW amendment. Current project context confirms no formal extension approval is documented despite explicit timeline extension to October 30, 2026. The risk is critical because it creates legal exposure, payment ambiguity, and potential service gaps during the most critical delivery phases (PAT, Regression, Deployment, Hypercare). This risk is immediately relevant as the project enters UAT preparation with all remaining milestones occurring beyond the contractual end date.

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Critical Client Dependencies Blocking PAT and Regression Readiness
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Multiple high-severity dependencies on Vivli team remain unresolved as the project enters the critical PAT and Regression phases. Automation testing environment has not been provisioned since July 29, 2026 (15 days overdue), chat-based escalation requirements remain pending refinement, and Azure monitoring/alert process confirmation is outstanding. These unresolved dependencies threaten PAT entry readiness, testing completeness, and schedule adherence during the compressed 78-day remaining timeline.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Client-controlled environment provisioning, requirement clarification, and infrastructure configuration processes are not aligned with project critical path timing. Historical pattern shows Sprint 1 slipped by one week due to broader scope and client cloud environment dependencies. Current project exhibits the same dependency management weakness with multiple high-severity items outstanding for extended periods without escalation or resolution.

predictedRisks.riskTitle: PAT Phase Defect Volume Exceeding Resolution Capacity
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The 15-day Product Acceptance Testing phase (August 31 - September 18, 2026) faces high risk of discovering significant defect volume that cannot be resolved within the allocated window. Current project shows 33 open work items (62% of total 53 items), significant UI-related bugs, and bugs in in-flight functionalities. Historical pattern shows PAT feedback from Sprints 1-3 generated enhancement requests and defects requiring prioritization and incorporation into subsequent sprints. With compressed timeline, limited buffer (33 days total remaining), and critical Code Freeze on September 18, 2026, excessive PAT defects could force regression delay, deployment postponement, or quality compromise.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Accumulating technical debt with 33 open work items, late front-end testing focus resulting in significant UI bugs, and feedback-driven development model that defers some quality issues to PAT phase. Backend-first development approach with UI lag created user experience issues discovered late in cycle. Front-end automation resource mobilized only in Sprint 4 (Week 11), reducing early defect detection.

predictedRisks.reasoning: The risk is highly likely because current project already shows significant technical debt (33 open items, 62% of total), UI-related bugs constitute a significant percentage of defects, and bugs exist in in-flight functionalities. Historical evidence shows PAT phases generate substantial feedback requiring prioritization and sprint incorporation, and extended PAT duration was added post-initiation suggesting original scope was insufficient. The risk is high-impact because PAT is a 15-day critical path activity with Code Freeze immediately following, leaving no buffer for overrun. With only 33 days of total buffer remaining and 30 days of formal testing (PAT + Regression) ahead, excessive PAT defects would consume all available schedule contingency and force deployment delay. The feedback-driven development pattern, while positive for quality, creates risk of late-stage defect accumulation when timeline compression limits resolution capacity.

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Regression Testing Defect Discovery Forcing Deployment Delay
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The 15-day Regression Testing phase (September 21 - October 9, 2026) represents a critical quality gate where comprehensive end-to-end validation may uncover integration defects, performance issues, or functionality regressions requiring resolution before deployment. With Code Freeze on September 18, 2026 and deployment scheduled for October 10-16, 2026, any significant regression defects discovered would leave minimal time for fixes, re-testing, and deployment preparation. The compressed timeline provides only 1 day between regression completion and deployment start, creating high risk of deployment postponement if regression issues emerge.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Regression testing was added after project initiation and not part of original SOW, indicating late recognition of comprehensive testing need. Original 16-week timeline did not account for formal regression phase. Current technical debt, UI issues, and in-flight functionality bugs increase probability of regression defects. Integration points (Azure services, Vivli platform, escalation workflows, monitoring/alerting) create multiple failure modes requiring validation.

predictedRisks.reasoning: The risk is medium-high likelihood because regression testing is a comprehensive validation phase where integration issues, performance problems, and functionality regressions are typically discovered. Historical evidence shows regression testing was added post-initiation, suggesting it was not fully planned in original timeline. Current project context shows technical debt, UI issues, pending technology migration (GPT-5 Mini), and multiple integration points (Azure services, Vivli platform, escalation workflows) that increase regression defect probability. The risk is high-impact because regression completion on October 9 leaves only 1 day before deployment start on October 10, providing no buffer for defect resolution. Any significant regression issues would force deployment delay, extending the project beyond the already-extended October 30 completion date and requiring additional contract extension. The compressed timeline between regression and deployment creates a binary outcome: either regression passes cleanly or deployment must be postponed.

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Production Deployment Failure or Rollback Requirement
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The 5-day production deployment window (October 10-16, 2026) faces elevated risk of deployment failure, partial deployment, or rollback requirement due to compressed preparation time, unresolved dependencies, technical complexity, and limited deployment buffer. Deployment occurs immediately after regression completion with no contingency window. Critical dependencies (Azure monitoring/alerting, escalation workflows, environment configuration) may remain incomplete. Integration with Vivli's existing platform, Azure infrastructure provisioning, and production environment readiness represent multiple failure modes. User training scheduled during deployment (October 14) creates additional coordination complexity.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Compressed deployment timeline with only 5 days allocated for production deployment of complex AI-powered solution with multiple Azure service integrations. Unresolved dependencies (Azure monitoring, escalation workflows, environment provisioning) threaten deployment readiness. Original 16-week timeline allocated only 1 week (Week 14) for deployment, indicating underestimation of deployment complexity. No documented deployment rollback plan or contingency procedures in evidence.

predictedRisks.reasoning: The risk is medium likelihood because production deployments of complex AI solutions with multiple Azure service integrations inherently carry deployment risk, and current project shows unresolved infrastructure dependencies (Azure monitoring, environment provisioning) that threaten deployment readiness. The compressed timeline provides no buffer for deployment issues, creating binary success/failure outcome. Deployment represents the highest-risk single event in remaining project timeline.

predictedRisks.reasoning: The risk is medium-high likelihood because escalation requirements remain pending refinement as of August 10, 2026, just one week before Sprint 5 begins on August 17. Historical evidence shows broader scope than expected caused Sprint 1 slip, and current project exhibits scope refinement during execution. Escalation workflows are complex integrations spanning Form Check, Agentic Chat, and Vivli platform with human reviewer interfaces. The risk is medium-high impact because escalation capability is a core SOW deliverable for both use cases, and incomplete escalation would represent failed acceptance criteria and operational gaps. Escalation workflow issues discovered during integrated workflow demo (August 28) or PAT would delay acceptance and potentially require significant rework. The timing of escalation integration in Sprint 5 with requirements still being refined creates high probability of incomplete or inadequate implementation.

recommendations.preventive: Complete escalation requirements refinement immediately (by August 16) to enable Sprint 5 development; conduct comprehensive escalation workflow design and validation before implementation; engage Vivli stakeholders early to ensure escalation procedures align with operational processes; allocate adequate Sprint 5 resources to escalation workflow implementation given its criticality as core SOW deliverable.
recommendations.monitoring: Track escalation requirements refinement completion status daily; monitor Amruta-Sarah discussion outcome and requirements documentation progress; track escalation workflow implementation progress during Sprint 5; measure escalation workflow testing coverage and validation status; maintain escalation workflow risk dashboard.
recommendations.contingency: If escalation requirements cannot be finalized by August 16, implement basic escalation workflow in Sprint 5 with post-PAT enhancement for advanced features; if escalation workflow implementation cannot be completed by Sprint 5 end (August 26), extend Sprint 5 by 3-5 days with corresponding integrated workflow demo and PAT delays; if escalation workflow validation fails during integrated demo or PAT, prepare remediation plan with extended development and testing or conditional acceptance with post-deployment completion.
recommendations.strategic: Implement requirements management discipline requiring critical integration requirements (like escalation workflows) to be finalized early in project lifecycle; strengthen scope definition and requirements sign-off processes to prevent late-stage requirement refinement; establish integration complexity assessment early to ensure adequate implementation time allocation.
